correctness.rationale: The update has an explicit two-sided inverse. Exhaustive Python enumerates every one of the 196608 states, checks inverse and symmetry commutation, and obtains the full temporal and geometric cycle census. An independent C++17 implementation verifies bijectivity by indegree one, reconstructs all primitive periods, and computes symmetry-class counts via Burnside fixed-cycle sums. Both outputs agree on every one of 20 table rows, the 2480 cycles, 74 symmetry types, and all boundary conditions. The assertions are finite exhaustive statements and make no larger-grid inference.

originality.rationale: The exact 20-period primitive-cycle population, 48-element geometric quotient and 74 symmetry classes for all 196608 states of the 3-by-4 ordinary torus are not implied by the checked prior statements. The most relevant prior explicit entry is the periods 72 and 56 of a uniform board under different initial heading axes; general reversibility and line-parity bounds only constrain possible cycles. Primary material on the infinite lattice and twisted tori addresses different domains. Unindexed enumeration remains a residual historical risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed or unpublished small-grid exhaustive enumerations may contain the same table; search absence does not certify historical priority.

value.rationale: The 3-by-4 torus is the smallest unequal-sided periodic square lattice with at least three sites in each direction; loss of quarter-turn symmetry motivates its geometric classification. The exact 2480-cycle census and its 74 geometric types address a natural complete finite dynamical invariant not determined by previously reported uniform-board periods or generic parity bounds. Period 72 alone contains 18 inequivalent geometric types while the maximum period 312 contains exactly two, proving that temporal period does not classify the orbit geometry in this first rectangular case. No unproved all-size significance is asserted.
